newsitem.title: USA: McDonald's Q3 U.S. operating income drops.
newsitem.headline: McDonald's Q3 U.S. operating income drops.

text.p: McDonald's Corp said Friday its U.S. operating income declined five percent in the third quarter, compared with a two percent increase in the 1995 third quarter.
For the first nine months of the year, U.S. operating income declined three percent, compared with an increase of three percent in the 1995 period.

U.S. systemwide sales in the third quarter rose two percent, compared with a five percent gain a year ago. McDonald's said its U.S. revenues in the quarter rose one percent, compared with a six percent rise a year ago.
McDonald's said restaurant expansion was responsible for increasing U.S. sales as 899 restaurants were added in the last 12 months.
Comparable-store U.S. sales, measuring results from units open at least a year, declined for the third quarter and nine months, it said.
McDonald's said U.S. results were hurt by an "extremely competitive" operating environment and, at times, difficult comparisons and bad weather.

The company said decreases in U.S. operating income for both the quarter and nine months reflected lower margin dollars at company-operated stores and higher general, administrative and selling expenses. This was partially offset by higher franchised margin dollars.
Higher operating expenses also contributed to the nine-month decrease, it said.
Despite the drop in U.S. results, McDonald's said it expects record earnings for the year.

"We are confident in our growth strategies and expect 1996 to be another record-breaking year," Michael Quinlan, chairman, said in a statement. "We will use our growing cash flow and debt capacity to fund global expansion, pay dividends, and repurchase stock under our $2 billion, three-year program."
